page: OVHcloud c2-60 is a compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical Intel cores running at 3.0 GHz with a Haswell microarchitecture that lacks TSX support. The system is configured with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, providing 16 independent execution threads. It is equipped with 60.0 GB of RAM, yielding 3.75 GB of memory per core, and includes 400 GB of local SSD storage alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates that the server performs within the average tier for most multi-core operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score is 24461.89, and the PassMark CPU score is 24191.73. Single-core performance represents a relative bottleneck, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1093.0 and a text processing score of 1434.0, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested systems. However, multi-threaded operations show stable throughput, as evidenced by a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 142.69 GB/sec and a Redis SET performance of 25.27 million operations per second.

The instance demonstrates average performance in software compilation, scoring 15531.0 on Geekbench Clang, and static web serving at 16.25 GB/sec. Large language model inference represents a clear performance tradeoff; while prompt processing for a 7B model achieves an average speed of 34.69 tokens per second, text generation on the same model drops to a weak 6.54 tokens per second. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded compute workloads, database operations, and static web serving, rather than single-threaded tasks or large-scale AI inference.
